records.markdown:
### CON-ARCH-003 — Tooling artifact authority and derived-state boundaries

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | constraint |
| Target | v2.3.0 |
| Status | planned |
| Priority | critical |
| Tags | v2.3.0, architecture, workflow, derived-cache, lock |
| Risk | high |
| Stability | evolving |
| Verification Method | test, inspection |
| GitHub Issue | - |
| Related Docs | [docs/research/230.md](../research/230.md), [docs/research/230plus.md](../research/230plus.md), [docs/research/10.kiwi-planner-jsonl-tooling-research.md](../research/10.kiwi-planner-jsonl-tooling-research.md) |

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi v2.3.0 must define product-level authority boundaries for SRS Markdown, workflow artifacts, derived caches, and lock files so tool-improvement features do not create alternate requirements sources of truth or ambiguous operational state.

#### Rationale

The 10-axis SRS usefulness review found that v2.3.0 introduces workflow JSONL, derived status cache, and lock files but the architecture scope still only describes the v1.0.0 Markdown/core boundary.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: docs/spec Markdown remains the only canonical requirements source; workflow artifacts such as plans, pipeline JSONL, sessions, PM state, coder state, and worklogs are operational inputs or audit artifacts, not canonical Requirement Blocks.
- [ ] AC-2: kiwi/.status.json is treated only as a disposable derived cache; missing, stale, or corrupt cache content triggers canonical parsing fallback and visible diagnostics or regeneration metadata.
- [ ] AC-3: kiwi/.srs.lock or the documented successor lock file is the authoritative SRS mutation exclusion mechanism; deleting or regenerating derived cache files never releases an active lock.
- [ ] AC-4: CLI, MCP, and skill-facing workflow projections report artifact source kind, path, workspace root, and hash or mtime when combining SRS and workflow state.
- [ ] AC-5: Tests or inspection cover no alternate requirements source creation, cache corruption fallback, lock/cache separation, and workspace-boundary behavior for mixed SRS and workflow artifact reads.

#### Verification Evidence

| Evidence ID | Type | Reference | Covers | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Trace Links

| Type | Reference | Relation | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Requirement | CON-ARCH-001 | extends | Preserves Markdown as the only requirements source of truth. |
| Requirement | CON-ARCH-002 | extends | Refines no-database/local-first behavior for derived caches and workflow artifacts. |
| Requirement | FR-NODE-020 | depends_on | Workflow artifact resolver consumes the boundary. |
| Requirement | FR-NODE-021 | depends_on | JSONL utilities operate on operational artifacts, not Requirement Blocks. |
| Requirement | FR-NODE-027 | depends_on | Status cache is derived and disposable. |
| Requirement | REL-NODE-005 | depends_on | SRS lock remains authoritative over mutation exclusion. |
| Requirement | REL-MCP-003 | depends_on | Workspace identity is required when mixing artifacts. |

#### Research / Analysis

- Doc230 established that `kiwi/.status.json` can speed up Requirement ID allocation but must remain disposable: missing or corrupt cache state falls back to canonical SRS parsing, and regeneration cannot make the cache authoritative.
- Doc230 Plus and the planner JSONL research distinguish operational workflow artifacts from Requirement Blocks. Plans, sidecars, pipeline JSONL, session state, and worklogs can guide execution, but they cannot replace `docs/spec` as the requirements source of truth.
- The 10-axis usability review found that cache, lock, workflow projection, and runtime skill migration requirements were individually useful but needed one product-level authority boundary so later CLI, MCP, and skill work cannot create a second SRS store by accident.

#### Implementation Notes

- Keep this as the product-level boundary. Detailed behavior stays in FR-NODE-020, FR-NODE-021, FR-NODE-027, REL-NODE-005, and REL-MCP-003.

#### Change Notes

| Date | Change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-06-29 | Created | add-requirement |

| Field | Value |

| Related Docs | [docs/research/09.mcp-cli-tool-abandonment-research.md](../research/09.mcp-cli-tool-abandonment-research.md) |

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi MCP mutation schemas and handlers must expose the same dry-run, notes, diagnostics, and structured mutation-envelope behavior as the shared core mutation services for AC, evidence, trace, requirement, status, stability, target, and completed-work mutations.

#### Rationale

The research found that MCP AC, evidence, and trace mutation adapters can omit dryRun or notes even when the core supports them. Agents that trust MCP previews must not accidentally write files or lose evidence context.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: MCP schemas for check_acceptance_criteria, add_verification_evidence, and add_trace_link accept dryRun when the underlying core mutation supports dry-run behavior.
- [ ] AC-2: MCP handlers forward notes and dryRun for evidence and trace mutations and preserve dryRun for AC mutations.
- [ ] AC-3: MCP mutation responses expose the shared mutation envelope from FR-NODE-017, including written state, operation preview, diagnostics, and diagnosticsSummary.
- [ ] AC-4: MCP failure responses preserve core diagnostics arrays and diagnosticsSummary instead of returning only a code and message.
- [ ] AC-5: MCP parity tests prove dry-run calls leave fixture file hashes unchanged and notes round-trip exactly into Verification Evidence and Trace Links rows.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi MCP tools and resources must preserve diagnostics, diagnosticsSummary, remediation data, and adapter parity in both success and failure envelopes so MCP clients can recover from validation, lookup, mutation, and workflow-artifact errors without losing context.

#### Rationale

The research found that MCP failure conversion can strip diagnostics down to code and message. MCP-first workflows need the same diagnostic information as CLI and core responses.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: MCP success envelopes include ok, value, diagnostics, diagnosticsSummary, and any relevant metadata without changing the domain-specific value shape unexpectedly.
- [ ] AC-2: MCP failure envelopes include ok false, error code, message, diagnostics, diagnosticsSummary, and recoverable next-action hints when available.
- [ ] AC-3: MCP mutation failures preserve stale-patch diagnostics and validation diagnostics emitted by core mutation services.
- [ ] AC-4: MCP read, resource, mutation, and workflow-artifact tests cover diagnostics-preserving success and failure paths.
- [ ] AC-5: MCP envelope behavior remains compatible with existing resource payload policy while documenting any legacy compatibility mode separately.

records.title: MCP Requirement ID collision repair tools

acceptanceCriteria.text: MCP registers diagnose_requirement_id_collisions, plan_requirement_id_collision_repair, and apply_requirement_id_collision_repair tools or documented equivalent names. Diagnose and plan schemas include duplicateId, occurrence identity, replacementId or allocation strategy, reference policy, explicit reference edits, and dryRun but reject ignoreLock with diagnostics; only the apply schema may include ignoreLock.

The diagnose and plan tools are no-write by default and return grouped SRS-E002 diagnostics, occurrence identity, generated replacement ID candidates, ambiguous inbound references, provenance hints, and patch preview when a plan is requested.

records.title: Logical workflow deletion state

acceptanceCriteria.text: Workflow logical-delete mutation kinds can mark supported workflow records as `deleted` effective state without physically removing the original JSONL line, Markdown checkbox line, PM state record, or repair record.

Each logical-delete write records the target record identity, deleted state, reason, owner, timestamp, journalKey or idempotency key, stale guards, and source artifact hashes needed to prove what was deleted.

Default workflow read tools treat logically deleted records as inactive while preserving audit metadata, and expose an explicit includeDeleted or equivalent option for read/list/tail inspection and repair.

Logical-delete mutations reject stale artifacts, invalid record IDs, forbidden owners, malformed JSONL, dependency-blocked writes, attempts to delete records that are not in a deletable class, tombstone-of-tombstone, correction-of-tombstone, and plain deletion of `CORRECTION` events unless a future restore requirement defines safe semantics.

Logical-delete mutations are idempotent: deleting an already deleted record returns a successful no-op mutation envelope without writing a duplicate tombstone unless the caller explicitly requests a new repair note.

Pipeline logical-delete handling must not add `deleted` to the pipeline `status` enum; it must represent deletion as `status=CORRECTION` plus `operation.kind="logical_delete"` or an equivalent tombstone/repair record, and apply logical-delete tombstones before normal correction chains so directly tombstoned records cannot be resurrected by correction-of-correction.

Tests cover logical delete, already-deleted no-op, non-deletable record rejection, stale hash rejection, invalid JSONL rejection, read filtering, includeDeleted inspection, tombstone/correction-of-tombstone rejection, `status=deleted` rejection, and partial-failure repair reporting.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi must provide guarded logical deletion mutations for workflow artifacts that mark plan display records, PM task records, pipeline events, worklog events, and workflow repair records as `deleted` through append-only tombstone or repair records instead of physically deleting JSONL lines or Markdown history.

#### Rationale

Planner and JSONL artifacts are audit and resume evidence. Physical deletion can hide partial failures, break correction chains, and make the next agent hallucinate state. - [ ] AC-1: Workflow logical-delete mutation kinds can mark supported workflow records as `deleted` effective state without physically removing the original JSONL line, Markdown checkbox line, PM state record, or repair record.

- [ ] AC-3: Default workflow read tools treat logically deleted records as inactive while preserving audit metadata, and expose an explicit includeDeleted or equivalent option for read/list/tail inspection and repair.

- [ ] AC-5: Logical-delete mutations are idempotent: deleting an already deleted record returns a successful no-op mutation envelope without writing a duplicate tombstone unless the caller explicitly requests a new repair note.
- [ ] AC-6: Pipeline logical-delete handling must not add `deleted` to the pipeline `status` enum; it must represent deletion as `status=CORRECTION` plus `operation.kind="logical_delete"` or an equivalent tombstone/repair record, and apply logical-delete tombstones before normal correction chains so directly tombstoned records cannot be resurrected by correction-of-correction.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi core requirement mutations must use kiwi/.status.json as an optional derived cache for Requirement ID counters and SRS mutation status, while preserving docs/spec/**/*.srs.md as the canonical source of truth and falling back to full workspace parsing whenever the cache is missing, malformed, stale, or unsafe.

#### Rationale

Doc230 found that add_requirement currently scans all Requirement Blocks to generate IDs, which is robust but can become costly in very large SRS repositories. A repository-local derived cache can reduce repeated full scans without weakening Markdown canonicality.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: kiwi/.status.json stores schemaVersion, generatedAt, source, specFingerprint data, idCounters keyed by requirement type and scope prefix, and mirrored SRS lock status for diagnostics.
- [ ] AC-2: add_requirement validates cache schema, source, fingerprints, ID prefix mapping, and relevant SRS file freshness before using cached counters.
- [ ] AC-3: If the cache is absent, malformed, stale, incomplete, or unsafe, add_requirement falls back to the existing full workspace parse and does not fail only because the cache is unusable.
- [ ] AC-4: Before any write, the selected Requirement ID is rechecked against canonical parsed SRS records so discarded or existing IDs are never reused.
- [ ] AC-5: After a successful SRS mutation, SpecKiwi regenerates or atomically updates kiwi/.status.json; cache write failure after a successful SRS mutation returns success with diagnostics because the cache is rebuildable.
- [ ] AC-6: Tests cover valid-cache allocation, missing-cache fallback, malformed-cache fallback, stale-fingerprint fallback, final collision detection, atomic cache write, and cache-write warning behavior.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi workflow mutation services must use a canonical journal identity that includes workflow run identity, expose journal inspection as mutation evidence rather than a separate source of truth, and restrict repair application to recorded pendingRepair records with dry-run-first and stale-guard checks.

#### Rationale

Doc230 Plus found that existing workflow mutation requirements describe journalKey formulas that omit run_id, which can collide across repeated task IDs in different runs. The research also found that repair is useful only when it operates on explicit pendingRepair records instead of inferring fixes from plan display state.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The canonical workflow mutation journalKey is sha256(tool|run_id|task_id|req_id|canonicalJson(flat_args)), where req_id uses a documented empty stable token for non-requirement-scoped workflow operations.
- [ ] AC-2: Canonical JSON for journalKey calculation is deterministic across CLI and MCP adapters, including stable object-key ordering, normalized absent optional fields, and exact treatment of task_id, req_id, and run_id.
- [ ] AC-3: Core mutation responses expose journalKey, journalState, idempotencyKey, completedOperations, pendingOperations, pendingRepair, diagnostics, and diagnosticsSummary using the canonical identity from this requirement.
- [ ] AC-4: Journal inspection reports planned, applied, confirmed, failed, and skipped_dry_run states as audit evidence only and never outranks plan sidecar, PM state, worklog, or validator source-of-truth precedence.
- [ ] AC-5: Repair application is dry-run-first by default, applies only a recorded pendingRepair whose stale guards still match, and never infers repairs from unchecked plan boxes or deleted/corrected JSONL records alone.

records.title: Logical workflow deletion state with canonical mutation dependency

acceptanceCriteria.text: Workflow logical-delete mutation kinds can mark supported workflow records as `deleted` effective state without physically removing the original JSONL line, Markdown checkbox line, PM state record, or repair record.

Each logical-delete write records the target record identity, deleted state, reason, owner, timestamp, canonical journalKey or idempotency key, stale guards, and source artifact hashes needed to prove what was deleted.

Default workflow read tools treat logically deleted records as inactive while preserving audit metadata, and expose an explicit includeDeleted or equivalent option for read/list/tail inspection and repair.

Logical-delete mutations reject stale artifacts, invalid record IDs, forbidden owners, malformed JSONL, dependency-blocked writes, attempts to delete records that are not in a deletable class, tombstone-of-tombstone, correction-of-tombstone, and plain deletion of CORRECTION events unless a future restore requirement defines safe semantics.

Logical-delete mutations are idempotent: deleting an already deleted record returns a successful no-op mutation envelope without writing a duplicate tombstone unless the caller explicitly requests a new repair note.

Pipeline logical-delete handling must not add `deleted` to the pipeline status enum; it must represent deletion as status=CORRECTION plus operation.kind="logical_delete" or an equivalent tombstone/repair record, and apply logical-delete tombstones before normal correction chains so directly tombstoned records cannot be resurrected by correction-of-correction.

Tests cover logical delete, already-deleted no-op, non-deletable record rejection, stale hash rejection, invalid JSONL rejection, read filtering, includeDeleted inspection, tombstone/correction-of-tombstone rejection, status=deleted rejection, and partial-failure repair reporting.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi core must provide guarded diagnose, plan, and apply services for merge-time Requirement ID collisions caused by parallel worktree or branch SRS additions, while rejecting general renumbering and preserving Markdown SRS as the canonical source of truth.

#### Rationale

Doc230 found that kiwi/.status.json and generated-ID optimistic concurrency reduce collisions within one checkout but cannot prevent independent worktrees from generating the same ID before merge. Existing granular editing and lock requirements are prerequisites, not the repair workflow itself.

- [ ] AC-5: Ambiguous inbound references, Completed Work Log rows without explicit mapping, research and analysis files, pipeline logs, evidence notes, Change Notes prose, and arbitrary Markdown text are report-only by default and never rewritten by automatic inference.

#### Requirement

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi v2.3.0 skill migration work must cover both canonical repository skill sources and runtime-installed Kiwi skill mirrors discovered in the active checkout, or explicitly classify those mirrors as generated install outputs with a validated refresh path.

#### Rationale

The 10-axis SRS usefulness review found that current runtime skills are loaded from .agents/skills, while MIG-FLOW-003 and the implementation plan focused on canonical skills/codex sources and left installed mirrors out of scope.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Migration inventory identifies canonical skill source trees and runtime-installed mirrors such as .agents/skills when they exist in the active checkout.
- [ ] AC-2: Each runtime mirror is either included in migration validation or classified as generated output with a documented refresh command, source manifest, and no-manual-edit rule.
- [ ] AC-3: Shared resource references from runtime mirrors, including ../_shared/kiwi paths, are validated or explicitly blocked before claiming migration readiness.
- [ ] AC-4: Scanner tests or inspection compare canonical source files, install metadata, runtime mirror paths, and shared-resource availability so stale or broken installed skills cannot pass unnoticed.
- [ ] AC-5: Skill migration remains gated on official workflow tools being implemented and validated; until then, runtime mirrors may document degraded raw-file fallback only with captured diagnostics and follow-up requirement IDs.

#### Verification Evidence

| Evidence ID | Type | Reference | Covers | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Trace Links

| Type | Reference | Relation | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Code | .agents/skills/kiwi-pipeline/SKILL.md:1-40 | related_to | Observed runtime-installed skill mirror and shared-resource reference pattern. |
| Code | .agents/skills/kiwi-planner/SKILL.md:1-45 | related_to | Observed runtime-installed planner mirror and shared-resource reference pattern. |

#### Research / Analysis

- Current Codex skill discovery in this checkout loads Kiwi skills from `.agents/skills/**`, not only from the canonical `skills/codex/**` source tree.
- Earlier runtime mirrors contained `.speckiwi-skill-install.json` files with only `name`, `agent`, and `installedAt`, which was not enough by itself to prove source path, source revision, checksum, refresh command, or no-manual-edit policy. Current mirror manifests and the installer contract must preserve those provenance fields so a documented refresh path can reproduce the same metadata.
- Some runtime skill instructions reference shared resources through `../_shared/kiwi/...`; migration readiness therefore requires validating whether the installed mirror includes those shared resources, whether they resolve back to the canonical source tree, or whether the mirror must be refreshed.
- The implementation plan must treat runtime mirrors as first-class migration inputs or explicitly classify them as generated install outputs before declaring skill migration complete.

#### Implementation Notes

- Do not migrate runtime mirrors to proposed workflow tool calls before those tools exist. First make mirror/source identity and shared-resource resolution visible and testable.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi MCP must expose the workspace root it is using, explain the root source, and fail safely when a request would read or mutate the wrong workspace, including multi-root and optional per-call workspace scenarios.

#### Rationale

The research found that MCP root behavior is fragile for agents operating across workspaces. Agents need explicit proof that MCP calls are reading and mutating the intended project root.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: MCP exposes a workspace information tool and includes workspaceRoot, rootSource, index path, active target, package version, and diagnosticsSummary in every read and mutation result envelope, or returns a structured diagnostic when an older envelope cannot carry those fields.
- [ ] AC-2: MCP root resolution distinguishes explicit root, server process cwd discovery, auto-init root, and rejected outside-root inputs in machine-readable output.
- [ ] AC-3: Optional per-call workspace arguments, if supported, are validated inside the project boundary and fail closed outside the configured root.
- [ ] AC-4: Multi-root MCP tests prove tools do not read or mutate a sibling repository when root identity differs from the caller's intended workspace.
- [ ] AC-5: MCP docs and managed agent instructions require checking workspace identity before target-scoped reads or mutations in multi-workspace sessions, and tests prove individual tools do not silently omit workspace identity metadata.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi core mutation services must use an SRS-only atomic lock file for writes to docs/spec, SRS rule files, index rollups, and SRS mutation cache files, while mirroring lock state into kiwi/.status.json for diagnostics without making the cache the lock authority.

- [ ] AC-1: The authoritative SRS mutation lock is the separate atomic lock file kiwi/.srs.lock, not kiwi/.status.json.

- [ ] AC-3: Read-only operations remain available while a non-stale SRS mutation lock is active.
- [ ] AC-4: A non-stale active lock causes mutation attempts to fail fast with structured SRS_LOCKED diagnostics including owner, operation, request ID, acquiredAt, expiresAt, and retry guidance.
- [ ] AC-5: Stale locks are recovered deterministically after expiry, and explicit lock bypass records diagnostics without disabling stale patch guards, generated-ID collision checks, table-cell safety, trace validation, or SRS validation.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi diagnostics aggregation must deduplicate repeated diagnostics and preserve row-level line anchors and structured details for parser, index, target map, scope map, summary, and completed-work validation findings.

#### Rationale

The research found duplicated diagnostics and weak index line anchors. Agents need precise, non-duplicated diagnostics to recover by editing the right row or invoking the right tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Validation output applies a deterministic dedupe key using diagnostic code, file path, line when available, requirement ID when available, and message.
- [ ] AC-2: Index diagnostics for Target Map, Scope Map, Status Summary, Requirement Type Summary, and Completed Work Log include the offending row line when the row exists.
- [ ] AC-3: Human read output reports compact diagnostics when nonzero and JSON output preserves diagnostics and diagnosticsSummary consistently.
- [ ] AC-4: Regression tests prove malformed table diagnostics are not double counted when parser diagnostics and validator diagnostics are combined.
- [ ] AC-5: Diagnostics include structured details or recommended next action data for recoverable cases such as duplicate target rows, rollup drift, missing scope documents, and malformed completed-work report paths.

#### Requirement

SpecKiwi validation must report duplicate Requirement ID failures as grouped, repair-ready SRS-E002 diagnostics so agents can see every occurrence of a duplicate ID and invoke a guarded repair workflow without scanning raw Markdown manually.

#### Rationale

Doc230 merge-time collision research found that the current SRS-E002 duplicate-ID diagnostic proves a duplicate exists but does not expose all occurrences or stable block identity needed for safe repair planning.

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: SRS-E002 diagnostics group records by duplicate Requirement ID and include every occurrence with filePath, headingLine, title, target, status, stability, marker state when available, and a stable blockHash or equivalent block identity.
- [ ] AC-2: The diagnostics summary counts duplicate-ID failures deterministically without double-counting repeated aggregation while machine-readable output preserves the full occurrence list for each duplicate group.
- [ ] AC-3: Grouped duplicate-ID diagnostics include a recoverable next-action hint that identifies when a selected occurrence is required before repair planning can write anything.
- [ ] AC-4: Tests cover same-file duplicates, cross-file duplicates, discarded or draft marked duplicates, more than two occurrences for one ID, and the existing duplicate-id fixture upgraded to assert grouped diagnostic detail.
- [ ] AC-5: CLI and MCP validation JSON preserve grouped SRS-E002 details through diagnostics and diagnosticsSummary without requiring raw Markdown bodies by default.
